name: Harden main-tip integrity sweep: confirm-re-run a named failing test on the current tip before filing a red-main alarm (kill parallelism-flake false CRITICALs)

task_definition.title: Harden main-tip integrity sweep: confirm-re-run a named failing test on the current tip before filing a red-main alarm (kill parallelism-flake false CRITICALs)
task_definition.description:
The async main-tip integrity sweep (task 1832's deliverable, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py run_main_tip_sweep + its alarm-filing path) repeatedly files FALSE red-main escalations from load-induced parallelism flakes that are 3/3 GREEN on isolated re-run, while main keeps merging cleanly. Recurrence is chronic: esc-main-sweep-ea2bd3c95e33-2 records 3 false alarms in ONE rotation on orchestrator/tests/test_concurrent_verify_boundary.py::test_concurrent_verify_boundary (B7/B4b/B6, all 3/3 green on re-run); a 2026-07-09 incident recorded 2 more false born-at-L2 CRITICALs (park_stop@324d09c742 + symlink-loop@935c, both 3/3 pass on re-run). These are the same load-sensitive xdist-contention flake class as done tasks 1836/1851/1925/2320/2350.

HARM: false CRITICAL red-main alarms are high-severity L2 noise and — worse — a false CRITICAL can prompt a defensive main ref-move; the standing operator rule is "NEVER ref-move on a sweep critical without re-running the named test on current tip first." The sweep should encode that rule itself instead of relying on a human to re-run by hand.

FIX (confirm-before-alarm gate, precedented by task 1690's merge-verify main-health re-probe): when the full-suite sweep run reports a test FAILURE (assertion failure OR pytest-xdist worker crash / "node down: Not properly terminated"), before filing any red-main escalation, re-run JUST the named failing test id(s) against the SAME current main tip in isolation (-n0, addopts cleared, small bounded retry e.g. up to 2 attempts). Only file the red-main alarm if the isolated re-run still fails on the current tip. If the isolated re-run passes, suppress the alarm and instead emit a non-blocking INFO/log note ("sweep flake suppressed: <test id> failed under load, passed on isolated re-run at <sha>") so the flake is still visible for de-flaking without paging a human.

Coordinate with pending task 2365 (treat pytest-xdist worker crash as a transient verify-infra error worth one auto-retry) — that fix is at the orchestrator per-task verify layer (workflow.py _run_verify_with_infra_retry); THIS task is the distinct main-tip integrity SWEEP layer (verify.py run_main_tip_sweep + the sweep's own alarm-filing path). Do not conflate the two subsystems; the sweep needs its own isolated-re-run confirm gate.

CONSUMER (G1): the human reading the orchestrator L2 escalation queue — they must stop receiving false red-main CRITICALs that are green on re-run. LEAF SIGNAL: a sweep run whose only failures are isolated-re-run-green files ZERO red-main escalations (emits an INFO suppression log instead); a genuine red (fails on isolated re-run at the same tip) STILL files the alarm — cover both with a regression test that injects a flaky-then-green fake test result and a genuinely-red fake test result.
